EventItemMinutesNote:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Michael James, Assistant County Manager, and Michael Haley, Executive Director and Wake County Economic Development Senior Vice President, shared the presentation. \par
\par
Mr. James shared the Business Development Grant Policy Recommendations\par
He shared the Policy Goals and Objectives.\par
He shared the Policy History. \par
He shared the Policy Results: Active Agreements.\par
He shared Wake Pays for Performance.\par
He shared the "Clawback" Provisions. \par
He shared Board Discussions.\par
\par
Michael Haley shared Proposed Changes.\par
He shared Adjust Wage Thresholds.\par
He shared Reduce Number of Project Tiers.\par
He shared Establish Transformational Project Tier.\par
He shared Decrease State Match Minimum.\par
He shared Adjust HQ Policy Tier Structure.\par
He shared Targeted Growth Areas.\par
He shared Policy Summary with Proposed Changes.\par
\par
Commissioner Stallings shared that this is a real value to the board and that we should always think about economic opportunities and economic mobility for our residents. She shared that Wake County wants to create as many economic opportunities for residents as they can. She shared that sometimes it is a misconception that the payout is at the front, but the payout does not occur until performance measures are met, and that we do have clawback measures in place to safeguard the dollars that the board is stewards of. \par
\par
Commissioner Thomas shared that, as Chair of the Economic Development Committee, they have been talking about this for quite some time. She shared that Mr. Haley and Mr. James have been listening to their feedback and have made the tweaks and changed some of the language. She shared that her question is about the adjusted wage thresholds. She shared that when it says the employer promotes economic upward mobility, what is the difference between promoting economic mobility and demonstrating that they already provide economic mobility. \par
\par
Mr. Haley shared that when they provide the board with project summaries, they want to give real examples from the company.  He shared that there is a strong policy and history of supporting economic development in Wake County. He shared that it has a lot to do with their policy and the strength of that, but also when working with these companies, it is often the case that they work with companies for months at a time before bringing an item to the board to talk about incentives at all.  He shared that they want to see demonstrated examples and history of the items. \par
\par
Commissioner Thomas asked if Wake Tech and Capital Area Workforce Development were involved in every conversation around economic mobility.  Mr. Haley responded that they are.\par
\par
Commissioner Evans shared that she feels like they have made the dollars and wage ranges relevant to current times rather than years ago, and that is reflected in the transformational projects as well because that's just a whole scope of project that they did not dream of seven to eight years ago.  She shared that when the board is reviewing a potential business that wants to come to this area, and they share that they want to offer a certain number of jobs, a distribution list of jobs is shared by Mr. Haley and Mr. James, so the board has been very focused on economic mobility for years. She shared that Wake County was known for years as a high-tech area, but not everyone benefited from prosperity. She shared that the board looks at the whole spectrum of jobs. She shared that she is proud of all the work done and what we do. She shared that she is happy to support the changes. \par
\par
Vice-Chair Jackson shared that we have reached a place of flexibility and balance with our values and are positioned to seize what is happening right now. She thanked them for bringing back the active agreement. She asked how they verify or ensure the headquarters strategy. \par
\par
Mr. Haley shared the appreciation. He shared that they set community expectations on how companies reflect the broader Wake County economy and community. When they work with headquarters, they make sure that they really understand the great array of existing companies headquartered here in Wake County and are long-standing advocates.  \par
\par
Commissioner Adamson shared comments on the priority growth areas. She shared that living wage jobs and barriers are education. Put companies that offer upward mobility in their community; not only are they able to get there, but it cuts down on traffic, and the closer you are to your job, the less you drive to get there. It cuts down on everyone's expenses, especially in a low-income area.  \par
\par
\par
\par
\par
}
EventItemActionText:
Commissioner Thomas moved, seconded by Vice-Chair Jackson, that the Board of Commissioners approve the updated Wake County Business Development Grant Policy to establish a Transformational Project Tier, create a job-based payout structure for Headquarters projects, and make adjustments to wage thresholds and the minimum investment for County participation in State Match projects. 

The motion carried by the following vote:

EventItemMatterName:
Michael James, Assistant County Manager
Michael Haley, Wake County Economic Development

EventItemMinutesNote:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;\red255\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Allison Cooper, Senior Assistant County Attorney, shared the WakeMed/Atrium Proposed Combination: Role of the Wake County Board of Commissioners. \par
\par
She shared the Overview.\par
She shared the WakeMed History as a County Hospital.\par
She shared Key Wake Memorial Hospital/WakeMed Events. \par
She shared the Transfer Agreement Reversionary Interest in WakeMed Real Estate. \par
She shared the impact of the 1997 Transfer/Sale.\par
\par
Tiffany Campbell, Senior Assistant County Attorney, shared the Governance Documents Under Consideration.\par
She shared What Changes for the County: Key Categories.\par
She shared Why the County Still Has a Role.\par
She shared Confidentiality: Competitive Healthcare Information.\par
She shared The County's Charge.\par
\par
\par
Chair Mial opened the Public Hearing.\par
\par
Dwight Spenser - thanked the board for delaying the vote to allow citizens to weigh in and for citizens to learn more. WakeMed has done its part in educating the residents. He shared that this is the people's hospital. \par
\par
Rob Stephens - Men of Southeast Raleigh: community questions have not been answered, and communication keeps coming in. He shared that the board will be self-handpicked. It's a marriage where one party owns the other. Redact trade secrets. \par
\par
Jamila Headley - shared that she spoke to a patient with pancreatic cancer and was here today to share his story. She shared that  Atrium stonewalled his care. \par
\par
Helen Sporkin - shared comments on experience at UNC. Not in favor of Atrium.\par
\par
Dickson Capps - shared that hospitals intimidated physicians; he shared that only 12 to 15 % cost transferred to the community. Not in favor.\par
\par
Nathan Foster - NC Justice Center, takeover will raise prices; Atrium will not treat the community right; shared statistics on Atrium.\par
\par
Emma Freer - block the merger. \par
\par
Aaron Daum - not in favor of the merger.\par
\par
Thomas Finke - Member of Atrium Health Foundation, shared comments of Atrium Healthcare, shared he has seen the commitments at Atrium. He supports the merger.\par
\par
Ardis Watkins- Exec, State Employee of NC; the employees are opposed to any merger with Atrium. Shared comments on the three commissioners meeting together so they would not be heard to the public records request.\par
\par
Ron Pringle - support should come with promises made; should be durable commitments; how will WakeMed patients be protected, charity care.\par
\par
Crister Brady - Family Physician, patients are challenged to pay bills, food, etc. WakeMed offers 12% charity care; Atrium offers 17%; means deferred care; no to Merger.\par
\par
Tchernavia Montgomery - Social Worker in Mecklenburg Co., serves 10,000 residents, in favor of merger.\par
\par
Harold Mallette - WakeMed is not the issue; it's the strategic partners, concern with Atrium and what the partnership will mean. Why give up control? Opposed to merger; if they vote yes, the decision made today will have an impact tomorrow.\par
\par
Cristin DeRonja - Significant steps should be taken to help create the WakeMed partnership.\par
 \par
Sam Hassell  - Cary, what has Atrium offered that is good for the citizens of Wake County. We would be giving Atrium a deal; haven't heard a resident say this is a good deal. Why do this deal.  It is a mega hospital grab, not interested in preserving care in Wake County. Vote no.\par
\par
Bob Winstead - will the people of Wake County be better off, not in favor.\par
\par
Carol Hardison - in support of Atrium Healthcare. \par
\par
Jessica MacDonald - in support of the merger. \par
\par
Mary Ann Baldwin - WakeMed provides excellent care; they are committed to their mission, in favor of merger.\par
\par
Woody Washam - former Mayor of Cornelius, in favor of merger, shared that Wake County can benefit.\par
\par
Jim Brennan - problem is lack of information, not being transparent, more information would be helpful.\par
\par
Mary Rider - residents benefit from WakeMed; WakeMed is a safety net; concerned with the takeover. \par
\par
Karen Dubose - Charlotte, shared comments on the Pearl, thriving black neighborhood, 5% affordable housing met with eight armed guards at a location. \par
\par
Jasmine Everett - Atrium Health, in favor of Atrium healthcare; they offer programs, 2 orgs with shared belief.\par
\par
Clara Hazlette-Norman - reject the takeover, shared remarks from someone at WakeMed, troubled by lack of transparency.\par
\par
Jerome Brown - Resist changes and don't enter agreements; adopt a no-compromise approach.\par
\par
Adwoa Asante - WakeMed saved her husband's mother; Atrium takeover puts us at risk; not in favor.\par
\par
Eilidh Reynolds - make deal public and vote no; do not sign away power.\par
\par
Anthony Trotman -Charlotte, in favor Atrium Health and their commitment to the community; shared comments on Gene Woods and what he has done for the community. WakeMed can benefit from the partnership.\par
\par
Stephen Morris- Mayor of Concord, relationship with Atrium.\par
 \par
Braxton Winston - former Mayor Pro Tem of Charlotte, disturbing pattern from Atrium Healthcare, not in favor of merger, CEO makes millions and employees are struggling.\par
 \par
David Smoot - challenging opportunity, asked board to extend the number of board members from 8 to 10, need a clear matrix.\par
\par
Lucy Mitchell - shared comments on Atrium Health. \par
\par
Terrence Dewberry - WakeMed is a place to go to; trying to figure out what's in it for him; opposed.\par
\par
Patricia Walker - WakeMed is important to the community, concerned about the lack of transparency, does not approve the deal. Put on ballot in November, forward together.\par
\par
Ronella Eaddy - Chief Nursing Officer, Atrium Health, in favor of merger. \par
\par
Julia Peter - NS\par
\par
Adelaide Martin - Charlotte, in favor of the Atrium Health merger.\par
\par
Harold Rice, Jr - Davidson, Atrium strong partner; Wake County will benefit.\par
\par
Alison Paladino - Cabarrus Regional Commerce, Atrium has been a contributor and brings key leaders to the table; Wake County has an opportunity to benefit.\par
\par
Dani Moore, Raleigh, concerned about Atrium taking over WakeMed, what will happen to underinsured.\par
 \par
Pastor Dennis Williams - Faith Memorial Church, Village Heartbeat, worked with Atrium Health, supported community health, mobilized churches during COVID, supports proposed partnership.\par
\par
Dr Andrea Fernandez - Chief Medical Officer at Atrium Wake Forest, shared statistics, improved access for all, supports the merger.\par
\par
Khaleel Faheemud-Deen - Raleigh, asking board to be transparent and make sure deal is good for all residents, vote no.\par
\par
Rev Frank Thomas - Mt Zion, High Point, had the same experience in High Point; healthcare is about people, build what the community needs, support stronger hospitals and communities.\par
\par
